paper.title_en: Geometry-Driven Suppression of Fermionic Pairing on a Spherical Surface
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the ground-state properties of a two-component attractive Fermi gas confined to a spherical surface. In the strongly attractive regime, the system forms a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of tightly bound dimers, yielding a gap and chemical potential that approach flat-space results with leading-order geometric corrections. As the attraction decreases, the system crosses over into a Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) regime, the sphere radius $R$ constrains the Cooper pair size and shell effects emerge. For closed shells, corresponding to magic particle numbers set by the single-particle spectrum, pairing is suppressed above the scattering length $a^*=4R$, whose value is universal in the spherical geometry in contrast with box-trapped fermionic gases. Our results highlight a fundamental interplay among geometry, quantum statistics, and interactions, motivating future experiments with shell-trapped ultracold fermions and inspiring geometry-controlled condensed matter devices.
